items.fact: The campaign is split into five chapters, and PC Gamer counts 91 story missions in total.

Other outlets count the story differently: Push Square and Insider Gaming both say 93 story missions across the five chapters, and GamesRadar says "over 90". The totals differ because some missions are optional.

Chapter 1 has 22 missions and is centred on the Leonida Keys. Chapter 2 is set in Port Gellhorn with 11 missions plus 2 optional ones. Chapter 3 is the longest, with 26 missions plus 1 optional, and moves to Vice City. Chapter 4 has 25 missions, and the final chapter has 7.
The five chapter titles are Just Like Paradise, Paradise Lost, Tits Ass Drug Money, Vice City, Baby, and Top of the World, Ma.
Chapters unlock in order once you finish the previous one, and missions can't be replayed after you complete them.
You play Jason and Lucia. In Chapter 3 you can finally switch between them, and Chapter 1 is Jason only.
In Vice City the pair work for employers including Dre'Quan Priest, Boobie Ike and Raul Bautista.
Collectible cards are spread across the five counties of Leonida, and finding three cards in each county unlocks the Collectible Cards achievement.
Gang hideouts, smash-and-grab spots, banks and payday loan shops show on the map index, and hovering over one shows its potential score.

There are 18 collectible card sets. Most have 24 cards, the Vice City Club de Futbol set has 30, the Backyard Wrestling set has 12, and the Delights set has 18. The Jack of Hearts, Nine1Nine, Legends of Ratface, Right Wing and ED Comics sets have 36 each.
100% completion requires 15 card sets, 30 magazines, books and comics, 200 base-model vehicles discovered, 50 standard-issue weapons, $100,000 of jewelry fenced and $250,000 of marked bills fenced.
The Progress menu tracks over 250 animal species, including 61 hunting animals, 60 birds and 35 fish.
There are 40 unique race locations. Entry and vehicle rental cost money, but winning pays more than you spend.
Demolition derbies at Ambrosia Raceway can be repeated, pay roughly $3,800 to $6,300 per win, and you win by default once every other car is wrecked.
As Jason you can scuba dive for buried treasure around Key Lento. Kenton gives you the approximate dive spots and eventually pays out tens of thousands of dollars if you find all the treasure.
From Chapter 2, Moses buys stolen cars that have no tracker, typically paying $1,000 or more. From mid-Chapter 3, Randy pays $30,000 or more for supercars from his 18-car wish list.
Bank vaults are the biggest earner, paying up to $200,000 at a time. You learn to rob them near the end of Chapter 4, and doing so instantly gives a 4-star wanted level.
Late in the game, respawning gang hideouts can pay roughly $10,000 to $30,000 per run.
You can scan a car with the Waink app to see its value. Pay 'n' Spray shops limit sales to about three or four cars a day, and sleeping resets the limit.
Don't rob banks or loan stores before Chapter 3. Their cash has dye packs, and you need a dye pack jammer to avoid the explosions.
For tougher robberies, invite your partner by pressing Triangle or Y on the map icon. Use the snap gun to get in through back doors without setting off alarms.
Buses and trains give cheap fast travel across Leonida, but they run on a schedule, so you have to wait for them. RydeMe is pricey early on.
Some PS5 players get error CE-108255-1 crashes, including at the opening prologue and during the Pipework mission. Reinstalling and rebuilding the database haven't fixed it for them.
The game has no dedicated first-person mode at launch. Players found a glitch that locks the camera in first person, and reloading your save undoes it.
